overall_diagnosis: Failures in the dialogue-parser task are most likely driven by unclear/incomplete guidance in dialogue-graph/SKILL.md (not the code) about (1) how edges serialize to the canonical wire format, (2) the exact exported JSON schema, and (3) precise rules for the reserved terminal target "End". The current documentation appears to contain truncation/wording issues and can mislead implementations into emitting wrong edge keys or incorrectly requiring/forbidding an explicit End node.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The “Adding Edges”, “Export”, and “End” convention documentation is ambiguous and/or internally inconsistent with the library’s actual behavior and the task’s expected JSON wire format. In particular: the mapping between Edge(source/target/text) and serialized edge dict keys {"from","to","text"} is easy to misapply; the top-level export schema (nodes/edges arrays) is not spelled out precisely; and the “End” convention is phrased too broadly and appears partially truncated, which can cause users to incorrectly treat non-End missing targets as valid or to always/never create a Node("End").
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction:
Edit dialogue-graph/SKILL.md to tightly align with Graph/Edge behavior and task expectations:
1) In “Adding Edges”, explicitly state: Python uses Edge(source=..., target=..., text=...), but serialization MUST use {"from": ..., "to": ..., "text": ...}. Provide one concrete JSON example of edges showing from/to/text keys.
2) Clarify the “text” field rule (match the task): whether it must always be present as a string (possibly "") or may be omitted; make this unambiguous and consistent with Edge.to_dict.
3) In “Export”, document the exact top-level schema: {"nodes": [ {"id","text","speaker","type"}, ... ], "edges": [ {"from","to","text"}, ... ]}. Include a minimal full export example.
4) Rewrite the “End” convention to be precise: only the literal string "End" is a reserved TERMINAL EDGE TARGET that may be referenced without adding Node(id="End"); all other edge targets must correspond to existing nodes; multiple incoming edges to "End" are allowed. If allowing an explicit End node, state it is optional (not required) and must not contradict validation rules.
5) Remove/repair any truncated/incomplete sentences in the End-related paragraph so the rule cannot be misread.
